module: Define the release and assessment boundary

lesson.title: Find the applicable date
lesson.summary: Use the date for the provision, not a single date for the entire course.

prerequisites.reason: The date lookup distinguishes the system route and applicable section.

blocks: A **provision-specific timeline** records which obligation applies to which system on which date. In the retained 27 July 2026 baseline, Article 113 gives a general application date of 2 August 2026 and several exceptions. Recheck the legal version for an actual release.

Chapter III **Section 4**, concerning notifying authorities and notified bodies, applies from 2 August 2025. Article 113(c) moves **Sections 1–3**, except Article 6(5), to 2 December 2027 for Article 6(2)/Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Article 6(1)/Annex I systems.

Chapter III **Section 5**, containing assessment, declaration, marking and registration provisions, is not expressly included in that Sections 1–3 postponement. Do not conclude that every conformity-related duty is postponed by the high-risk dates. Record the interacting provisions and seek a supported interpretation for a real transitional release.

Article 111(2) has an **existing-system transition** for qualifying high-risk systems placed on the market or put into service before the relevant Article 113(c) date: this Regulation applies only if significant design changes occur from that date, without prejudice to Article 5. The paragraph also sets a 2 August 2030 compliance deadline for providers and deployers of high-risk systems intended for public authorities. These are conditions, not a universal grace period.

For each case record first market/service date, classification route, intended public-authority use, later design changes and the provision being assessed. In these exercises a temporal question can produce **needs specialist review**, rather than an unsupported ready/not-ready verdict.

questions.prompt: A reviewer says Article 113(c) postpones all of Chapter III, including Section 5. What is missing?

options.blocks: A separate reading of Section 5 and the interacting dates.
options.reason: The specified exception does not expressly list Section 5.

options.blocks: Nothing; the exception names all of Chapter III.
options.reason: It expressly identifies Sections 1–3, with an additional exception.

options.blocks: Nothing; all provisions began in August 2025.
options.reason: Section 4's date is not the date for every provision.

options.blocks: Yes; 2030 applies to every existing private system.

options.blocks: Permanently prohibited because the date is uncertain.
options.reason: An unresolved transition is not itself an Article 5 prohibition.

options.blocks: Needs further evidence and a dated interpretation.
options.reason: The missing facts prevent a supported temporal conclusion.
